Package dev.opencollab.paletter.vanilla

Class BedrockBlockState

java.lang.Object
dev.opencollab.paletter.vanilla.BedrockBlockState
public final class BedrockBlockState extends Object
One state of a BedrockBlockType. A type creates each of its states once, so with(dev.opencollab.paletter.vanilla.BedrockState<T>, T) does not allocate.

Equality: equals always works. == works too for the states of vanilla types (the constants) and of registered custom blocks: a CustomBlock owns its type and states, and a palette it is registered in hands back exactly those (Palette#blockState(NbtMap, Lookup), ...). Two states are equal when their types are equal and they have the same values(), whichever version or palette made them: a state a preview palette decodes for a block the preview changed equals the constant's state with the same values (it is not == it). The states of a type made for an identifier the bundled data does not know are equal by value, not identical. Equal custom blocks registered by different layers each own their states; those are equal, not identical.

Canonical ids come from the canonical block ids of the Paletter (vanilla states) and Palette.runtimeId(BedrockBlockState) (vanilla and custom states). For a vanilla state both are an addition, not a hash lookup: the first state of its block plus the sum of each value's index times the stride of its property, computed once (Bedrock enumerates every block's states as the full product of its values; blocks that are not get a lookup table). Custom block states have canonical ids per layer lineage only.

Since:
1.0.0

    • raw

      public @Nullable Object raw(@NonNull BedrockState<?> state)
      Reads the value of a state property as Bedrock sends it, without converting it to the state's Java type. Unlike get(dev.opencollab.paletter.vanilla.BedrockState<T>), it never throws: a value of a newer Bedrock version that a state enum has no constant for is still read here.
      Parameters:
      state - the state property to read
      Returns:
      the value as in values() (Boolean, Integer or String), or null if the block does not have the state
